items.title: Over 50% of a major streaming service’s tracks come from DistroKid – and other revelations from UMG’s lawsuit
items.summary: UMG's lawsuit accuses the DIY distributor of "deceptive trade practices and blatant copyright infringement", and of flooding streaming services with AI-generated "slop. Source

items.title: Suno Confirms V6 AI Music Model Was Trained on User Creations as Sony and Universal File New Copyright Lawsuit
DistroKid’s $2 billion valuation based on it being a pipeline for AI slop and copyright infringement, says Universal
items.summary: Universal claims that distributor DistroKid achieved its recent $2 billion valuation by providing a pipeline for AI slop and copyright infringing music, to the detriment of artists and labels. It has filed a lawsuit accusing DistroKid of copyright infringement and unlawful deceptive trade practices

items.title: Lady Gaga Shouldn’t Get $230K ‘Consolation Prize’ After ‘Mayhem’ Lawsuit, Surf Brand Tells Judge
items.summary: Lost Surfboards tried and failed to sue the pop superstar for infringing its "Mayhem" trademark on her chart-topping album.

items.title: ASCAP names Jackson Wagener as Senior Vice President and Head of General Licensing
items.summary: He will oversee the team that licenses the organization's repertory of over 20 million musical works to restaurants, bars, fitness studios, live music venues, and other establishments that use music. Source

items.title: Outkast sue Ovrkast after he reneges on commitment to change performer name to something less confusingly similar
items.summary: Outkast have sued Ovrkast for trademark infringement. Rapper and producer Ovrkast admitted himself in a Rolling Stone interview last year that lots of people confuse the two artist brands. A company that manages Outkast’s trademarks says Ovrkast agreed to change his name by July, but then didn’t

items.title: Landmark termination rights ruling not the “copyright emergency” music publishers claim, songwriter tells US Supreme Court
items.summary: When America’s Fifth Circuit Appeals Court backed a songwriter-friendly interpretation of the termination right in US copyright law, the majors bought the song that prompted that ruling and asked the Supreme Court to intervene. The writer of that song has now urged the top court to not get involved

items.summary: In March, American producer Michael Smith pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, following accusations that he had botted his way to more than $10m in royalties for his AI-generated music. The post is from Music Ally .

tip.title: Sample sin licencia no se arregla con 'menos de 7 segundos'
tip.body: No existe una cantidad de segundos legalmente segura. Cualquier fragmento reconocible puede ser infracción, y necesitas dos permisos: el de la grabación (sello) y el de la composición (editorial).

tip.title: There is no safe 'under 7 seconds' rule for samples
tip.body: No number of seconds is legally safe. Any recognizable fragment can infringe, and you need two clearances: the master recording (label) and the composition (publisher).
